The '''1933 [[Turkish Football Championship]]''' was the fourth edition of the competition. It was held in October. [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]] won their first national championship title in their history by defeating [[İzmirspor]] 8–0 in the replay of the final match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.angelfire.com/nj/sivritepe/5758/TB.html|title=Türkiye Futbol Birinciliği|publisher=Erdinç Sivritepe|access-date=31 December 2017}}</ref> In the initial final match between Fenerbahçe and İzmirspor the latter were leading 1–0 in the first half. In the second half the referee awarded Fenerbahçe a penalty, which led to persistent protests of İzmirspor players. Eventually, İzmirspor supporters invaded the pitch and the match was aborted. The [[Turkish Football Federation]] decided that the replay was to be played on the home ground of the club which would be selected by draw and that a foreign referee would be assigned.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://macanilari.com/29.Ekim.1933_1933.Sezonu.Turkiye.Futbol.Birinciligi.Final.Grubu.Final.Maci.Fenerbahce.1-0.Izmirspor._Yarida.kaldi_-193319337007--.html|title=1933 Sezonu Türkiye Futbol Birinciliği Final Maçı|website=macanilari.com|access-date=31 December 2017|language=tr|archive-date=26 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171226020955/https://macanilari.com/29.Ekim.1933_1933.Sezonu.Turkiye.Futbol.Birinciligi.Final.Grubu.Final.Maci.Fenerbahce.1-0.Izmirspor._Yarida.kaldi_-193319337007--.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The 1933 final produced the most goals scored in a final during the history of the competition, exceeding the six scored in the 1927 final. The various regional champions competed in a group stage of five groups of three or four teams each, with the group winners qualifying for the final stage.
